How likely is it that a guy who is very smart, who won the genetic lotto when it comes to intellect, also made out well in terms of the genes that affect his body? As in, natural athleticism, height, and so on, factors that make men look "manly" instead of soft or weak. 2. How many smart kids are underdeveloped physically and socially because they never got into athletic, team based pursuits or other physical ventures that would've A) built up their bodies and B) taught them how to communicate with normal people instead of other eggheads? If a kid is very smart and pushed toward intellectual pursuits only, he may squander some of his genetic potential and never gain a taste for more physical things. In other words, he got the wrong kind of nurturing to develop to his full potential; it's not that his genes suck. I've met a lot of smart kids (smart, but not THAT smart) who never did anything physical that they didn't have to. Never lifted any weights, didn't even play outside after school. They could have the best physical genes in the universe and still be hollow chested faggots. No doubt they would never achieve full potential if they neglected physical pursuits their whole youth, but they'd probably still do just fine after they put in the several thousand hours of work most sports-playing kids do by age 18. So are genetics unfair? No, it's just in a normal population you'll have a lot fewer people who win twice than people who only won once, and of the two-time winners only some of them will be encouraged to pursue athletics (which has both physical and social benefits) along with whatever nerd stuff smart kids do. That goes the other way too; I've met guys who were obviously incredibly sharp (after getting to know them well), but who had also obviously never had much guidance in building up their minds. They came across as significantly less intelligent than they were because of the way they communicated and the odd gaps in their knowledge. P.S. Another point to consider when thinking about the people you've known in your own life in this context: how would you know how intelligent a properly socialized, well rounded guy was if he knew better than to act like an aspie? I mean you'd probably think he was smart, but you might have no idea he really had a +3 SD IQ. Very smart people who spend a lot of time around more average intellects learn how to communicate with them, and generally have no need to prove how smart they are because their intelligence is not the core of their identity. Contrast that with some kid who is really only good at math and science, who sucks at everything else, and thus has to prove how smart he is all the time so he will feel good about himself.

author: Speculation
text_post: I'm going to let Scott Alexander make an argument for me: Quote:What are the sorts of things we might trade off against intelligence? Perhaps fitness, height, attractiveness, health, longevity, social well-adjustedness? But in fact none of these trade off against intelligence, many are strongly positively associated with it, and in some the link has been proven genetic! People with high IQ tend to live longer. For example, a person with IQ 115 (85th percentile) is 20% more likely to survive to age 76 than an average person with IQ 100. One can of course posit many possible connections. Maybe high-IQ people are smart enough to eat healthy and exercise. Maybe rich people can afford both good schools and good doctors. Maybe good health behaviors protect the brain as well as the body and increase both IQ and longevity. But further investigation has cast doubt on all of these theories and strongly supports the hypothesis that no, the same genes that give you high intelligence also make you live longer. See for example the International Journal of Epidemiology: The Link Between Intelligence And Lifespan Is Mostly Genetic, which find genetics explain 95% of the correlation. A few of the genes linking intelligence and longevity may be already known; SSADH seems to be a contributing factor. My favorite study in this area, though, is one that is not yet complete: since all mammals are basically the same [citation needed] some London School of Economics researchers have developed an IQ test for dogs in the hope of checking whether the same correlation applies to them. Since canine intelligence doesn’t affect things like diet, exercise, or tobacco status, a positive correlation in them too would help solidify the finding. We’re still waiting on those results, but even without them the genetic hypothesis is looking pretty strong. People with high IQ tend to be taller. This is interesting since height is often used as a measure of health and fitness during childhood, and since taller people get a bunch of advantages including being rated as more attractive and earning higher income. Once again we can imagine all sorts of possible confounders; once again studies find that the link is genetic. See for example Common Genetic Variants Explain The Majority Of The Correlation Between Height And Intelligence, The Genetic Correlation Between Height And IQ: Shared Genes Or Assortative Mating, Resolving The Genetic And Environmental Sources Of The Correlation Between Height And Intelligence, On The Height-Intelligence Correlation. People with high IQ may be more attractive. This is the conclusion of a meta-analysis that finds a positive correlation between intelligence and body symmetry, usually used as a proxy for attractiveness unaffected by things like hairstyle and cosmetics; a second study failed to find this relationship. The jury is out on the positive link, but there certainly isn’t the negative link that Myers’ race car would predict. People with high IQ commit much less crime – which is going to be our measure for social well-adjustedness here since it’s well studied. Once again it’s easy to think of possible confounders (I’ll add lead levels to the usual lot). Once again the studies show that at least some of the effect is genetic – here’s one on low-IQ/antisocial-behavior correlation in children, and here’s one cleverly linking fathers’ criminal history to sons’ vs. nephews’ IQ and then throwing enough statistics at it to find that the relationship is genetic. Likewise, the relationship between high IQ and low drug abuse seems to be genetic as well. People with high IQ tend to be more physically fit. This is the conclusion of a study of 1.2 million Swedes. I don’t have any strong evidence that this relationship is genetically mediated (although Gottfredson on the fitness factor may be relevant here), I just want to note that, once again, there is less than zero evidence for Myers’ race car hypothesis. People with high IQ have lower rates of heart disease, stroke, circulatory diseases, and diabetes. Intelligence may or may not decrease cancer risk, but again contra the race car hypothesis, it certainly does not increase it. Sibling designs suggest that shared family environment during youth is not responsible for the benefits; differential socioeconomic status as an adult may be, but this status is itself likely caused be the intelligence differences. The above and certain experience from my own life leads me to believe that high IQ men don't necessarily look less alpha. The only thing I could say is that neuroticism (lets roughly call it anxiety/fear) is more common in high IQ people, but that doesn't mean high IQ people are likely to be neurotic. I also know many high IQ people that have mastered the art of appearing as 90-100 IQ Joe Everyman. Day to day though, to survive, being +3 SD above average intelligence? - Middle syllables are swallowed:  Camera = Camra, Beautiful = Bewdful, Different = Diffrent. - 'I' is sounded as an 'oi' sound within words in certain instances:  Time becomes 'toime', Pizza is 'poizza'. - 'Er' sounds become 'ah' in certain instances:  Poofter = Pooftah; Subwoofer = Subwoofah; Runner = Runnah. It's all performance that I can turn on and off as needed, depending on the audience. If I was being fussy with the Wine and Cheese set - note I didn't say Woine - I might say 'How are you doing today?' or 'What are your plans for the weekend.' In Bogan (think Redneck) Speak, this becomes "'ow ya garn, mate?  What ya up ta Sat'dee?" If an educated friend had just been visibly-knocked back by a girl, what might be "She left quickly.  What on earth did you say that offended her?" becomes this, in Bogan Speak: "Fark, whatdya say ya mad cunt?  That mole was off like a Dapto dog." Something like: "I'd love a beer, please.  I'm very thirsty" becomes "Giz a fucken tinnie mate, I'm as dry as a nun's cunt." As such, If I spun a yarn with youse cunts the way I do down the pub, you probably wouldn't make a lot of sense out of it: Quote:"So I'm down me local late last Fri'dee.  Been tryen to pull this bird for coupla hours.  Thinken I'm in there and she's ready ta back up on it but when I put the hard word on her she arcs right up n gets shirty with me then pisses right off. So I'm toey and busten for a slash, so head off to the dunny but I end up standin there for fucken yonks with an angry pissfat, ya know how it goes. So im standen there tryen to get the bugger to go down n the fucken door BANGS open.  Woulda heard it down Sydnee way mate, I tell ya.  Scares the fuck outta me so I turn 'round and its this old mole of a cleanah, and she cops an eyeful of me mungrel. Doesn't. fucken. bat. an. eyelid.  Just goes 'Ah, sorry darl.  Thought it were empty this toime a noight.' I go 'nah no worries luv.  Only be a tick.' The mole gives me this dirty grin and goes... she just goes... 'Well let me know if ya need me ta help ya knock the top off of it,' and shuts the door. I tell ya, I just about pissed meself laughen cause oim thinken if Old Mate were here, he'd be given me the elbow and sayen 'garn Bosch.  Nevah let a chance go boi ol' son.  So wot if shes fucken rotten enuff that she makes ya spew when ya on the job, ay?  She got a fucken mop, don't she?'" Sometimes my persona will slip in polite company, and I'll fire off a 'cunt' where it's obviously not required, or it will slip into my writing by accident.  Doesn't seem to happen the other way around.  (Note how I swallowed the 'it' there?  That a common tell of me being caught in-between worlds). I know what you're thinking:  sounds like a fuckload of work (slipping again).  This is the reality of being such a highly-intelligent man in a country where intelligence is despised and wanting a healthy sex and social life, because otherwise I'd read as somewhere between 'weird to insane' to roughly 83% of the population.  Even as a kid, the other children would say "You talk funny" whenever I opened my mouth, which meant social exclusion.  In my neighbourhood, you needed the protection of the group to survive, because a child alone was a target.  I simply adapted. To be honest, I see high intelligence as being largely-useless in Australia, and a huge social handicap.  The snobs may sneer at the working classes, but underneath their violent and feral tendencies, they're good people, whose dysfunction is far more understandable and healthier than anyone I've interacted with from the upper classes.

author: scrambled
text_post: The reason is genetic -- intelligent people are more likely to be well groomed and fit. That is, better brain = better body, the genes are related. Top 20% is also not quite a precise number, as intelligence is distributed on a bell curve; so perhaps you meant the 14% of people who are two standard deviations above the median; ("honors students" in the street phrase) But the 2% who are three standard deviations over, ("gifted students"), are these badly groomed and physically unfit? Could you tell the difference between the two student groups? I doubt it; I'd bet the gifted students are just brighter. Quote: However I'd be inclined to agree that the very top men are less masculine. I don't want to brag, but I have a 140 IQ (certified test) and lift and play sports and I'm pretty socially able despite being a mild introvert.  Being an introvert doesn't make one socially unable; it's being dumb that does.  "Certified test", when was this taken and which test was it? Very few adults know their current IQ, as IQ changes and a real test is rather lengthy and expensive to take. Quote:The 4 or 5 guys I know that are your typical 140+ IQ 'geniuses' are nice guys and I could talk to them for years about deep topics, but they're a bit weird and eccentric (hence the crazy professor stereotype) Better to say 145+, or three standard deviations above, 'highly gifted', yet there are so few of these it would be shocking if you know as many as five; it would be the equivalent of personally knowing 4-5 guys who are over 6'6" tall.  Weird and eccentric are two different views on the same thing, one is pejorative and the other less so; which is it? And what does being 'eccentric' have to do with not being masculine? Also, professors aren't crazy, even by stereotype; the stereotype is that they are old and absent minded. Nor do professors have that high of an IQ, because the bell curve is like a supermassive statistical black hole that drags all, no matter what their social reputation otherwise may be, toward mediocrity; there are around 1.54 million post-secondary instructors in the United States alone, which would far exceed even the total theoretical number of highly-gifted people.  The highest IQ profession is physician, but the IQ median there is still only a sub-gifted 126, the equivalent of an 'A' honors student who would be sweating bullets in a gifted classroom, trying to keep their grades up by receiving private tutoring on the side.
